added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run's own logs and artifact set. The run's declared write paths reach no test file (a docs evidence fragment and an SVG figure), and its manifest records baseline_suite and after_suite as null, so its logs contain no suite arm and no failing test id. The only non-zero exit in its logs is score_sample.log (exit 2), which is two DecisionsValidationError refusals ('role' probabilities sum to 0.9900, not 1) on two files both labelled out-of-scope O (sample indices 29 and 121); that is a decisions-endpoint rounding defect owned by the sibling relevance-live-repairs node, not a failure introduced by this revision. The reviewed head 667daf21f differs from its base ce47cc8b7 only in two docs paths (the evidence fragment and the figure, 394 insertions, 0 deletions), so no source or test under any suite changed and zero added failures holds by construction. Positive control on the instrument: the same grep for passed|failed|exit|error that returns no suite summary line does match score_sample.log's "errors": 2, so the search sees content that is present.

findings.text: follow-on: the scope anomaly is reported, not fixed — the reset and triage stages of `imas-codex discover code` did not honour `--path-prefix`, so the seven-prefix passes triaged 2311 jt-60sa CodeFiles in the run window and 1384 of them under /analysis/src/edas2, stamped during pass 2. I confirmed the command carried exactly the seven prefixes (recovered from the run stream: `imas-codex discover code jt-60sa --path-prefix ... x7 --focus equilibrium --min-score 0 --time 8 --reset-to discovered`) and that pass 2's `code_worker started facility=jt-60sa` at 02:10:01 is followed by `triage decision failed for /analysis/src/edas2/...` lines from 02:10:19 (12 in the pass-2 window). The node reported this honestly as the material follow-on; the underlying tool defect (reset/triage ignoring --path-prefix) belongs to a separate node and affects shared facility graph state, so the coordinator must adjudicate whether peers were disturbed.

follow-on: (nit) the section h2 reads "the seven-prefix JT-60SA trial ingested every required files" — number agreement ('every required file' or 'all required files'). Cosmetic only; the body text below it is correct, so it does not block.

follow-on: (nit) the pre-trial table leaves the by-status cell empty for /analysis/lib/eqdbms (5 rows) and /analysis/lib/JT60SAEQDB (0 rows), so a reader cannot see what the 5 eqdbms rows were at that point. The post-trial table fills the equivalent cell (ingested content 1, scored content 2, skipped name 2), making the pre-trial omission more conspicuous than it needs to be.

follow-on: (nit) the AUC measurement script lives only in the run directory and is not committed to the repo, so the 0.955 figure is reproducible from the repo tree only while the run directory survives. It is a one-shot trial probe, which the plan does not require be committed, so this is a durability nit rather than a gap; the fragment does name the command and the run directory.

item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed run's manifest reads status complete with two commits and four test_logs; it records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm, and its declared write paths reach no test file, so the added-failure pair is derived from the run's own logs (no suite arm, only the two out-of-scope decision refusals) and corroborated by the docs-only base..head diff.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the two-commit diff touches exactly the declared write paths (docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/relevance-trial.html and docs/figures/jt60sa-discovery-completion/relevance-trial/content_relevance_by_class.svg) and nothing outside them; no source, test, plan HTML, plan meta or plan version line was touched.

justifications.durability: The measurements persist where a later reader can reopen them: the AUC, per-file relevances, receipt-file statuses, MINPACK result and spend are written into the committed evidence fragment, and the raw artifacts (score_sample_results.json, named_files.json, prefix_counts.json, the pass logs and the code_jt-60sa.log) persist in the run directory. The scope anomaly and the two secondary follow-ons are recorded for adjudication rather than passed over. Two deductions: the AUC probe score_sample.py is not committed (remaining only in the run directory), so reproducing 0.955 from the repo alone is not possible once the run dir is collected; and the pre/post graph counts (371 in scope, 2311 triaged, 1384 under edas2) rest on Cypher queries whose raw output is not stored in the fragment or a query log, so they are single observations a reader cannot re-derive from the artifacts.
justifications.evidence: Strong and independently checked. I recomputed the AUC from the recorded per-file rows in score_sample_results.json and got 0.9552080170057698, byte-equal to the recorded summary, with 126 rows, 37 in-scope positives, labels L15 P15 G5 I2 S23 O66 and relevance range 0.03-0.97. I verified the two excluded files (indices 29 and 121) are both labelled O, so the exclusion does not bias the in-scope set; the fragment's claim that the refusals do not touch the in-scope set is correct. The five received files' ingestion, inpgeo.c at 0.60 and mgset0.f at 0.39 are all present in named_files.json, and MINPACK shows 8 files all status=skipped, 0 ingested — the declared negative control holds. The three pass summary lines (0 scanned/223 scored/86 ingested $0.07; 0/0/10 $0.00; 0/0/0 $0.00) and the edas2 triage events are in code_jt-60sa.log, and the exact scoped command is recoverable from the run stream. Two deductions: the graph counts are not backed by a stored query log (see durability), and the pre-trial 'route down' state is a single-observation narrative (five retries) that the fragment reports but cannot be re-measured now.
justifications.fit: The deliverable matches the node: one evidence fragment and one figure under the plan's evidence and figure directories, written in mechanism language with the command, the query and the run-directory paths named so a reader can check them. The figure is the mandated 1400px-wide canvas with a caption, no gridlines or decorative shading, project-absolute img src (/imas-codex/figures/...) and per-class points coloured in-scope blue against out-of-scope grey with the 0.5 threshold drawn. Deductions: the h2 has a number-agreement wart ('every required files'); the pre-trial table leaves one by-status cell empty; and the fragment carries two run states (blocked, then restored) in one section, which makes the boundary between pre-trial and post-trial numbers a little harder to read than a single-state report would be.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's job is §25's relevance-trial: a scoped JT-60SA run over the seven equilibrium prefixes, measured against the labels, in repeated --time 8 foreground passes. All four done-when clauses are met and I reproduced the headline metric exactly (AUC 0.955 >= 0.90) from the run's own recorded rows; the deployed path is genuinely exercised, not a re-run of the prototype — score_sample.py calls the deployed build_triage_state(..., with_content=True), build_triage_questions, triage_relevance (SCOPE_NOULS, which I confirmed exists in scorer.py) and acall_decisions on the discovery-relevance seat. The five required receipt files were ingested through the content arm and no MINPACK file was; inpgeo.c and mgset0.f are reported with their relevance; the spend is recorded. One deduction: the run's side effects exceeded its declared scope — the reset and triage stages triaged 2311 files in the window, 1384 outside the seven prefixes — a material uncontrolled effect on shared graph state even though it is caused by a tool defect and the node reported it honestly rather than concealing it.
justifications.reuse: The measurement reuses the deployed machinery rather than a bespoke scorer: build_triage_state, build_triage_questions, triage_relevance and acall_decisions, and the trial reuses the existing discover code pipeline, GraphClient and the shared run-directory artifact pattern. No new production code, no duplicated logic. One deduction: the AUC and precision/recall helpers are re-implemented inside the one-shot run script rather than shared from a test helper, which is acceptable for a throwaway measurement but means the metric definition lives outside the suite.
justifications.scope_discipline: The node kept to its write scope: the two-commit diff touches exactly the two declared docs paths and nothing else, and no plan HTML, plan meta or plan version line was edited. The commits are conventional with bodies, carry no AI attribution and name no plan, sprint or ticket identifier. The one qualifier is the run's graph side effects exceeding the seven prefixes, which I record as scope-discipline evidence against the tool rather than against the node's writes; the node surfaced it for adjudication, which is the correct handling of a defect it was fenced out of fixing.
